title: release 18.5.0: a shipped `!` narrowing (#33637 — `os audit verify` now fails on `listed_twice`) and ten other shipped changes have no 18.5.0 CHANGELOG line, because their changesets were still pending at the release commit — recurrence of #29957
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzj9DrVWXkq7joYHGB

**What happens.** The release commit of 18.5.0 is tag `@objectstack/spec@18.5.0`, at `b914e724`. It still holds 11 unconsumed changesets in `.changeset/`. Their commits (10:36–11:18Z) are ancestors of the tag, so their code is in the published 18.5.0 tarballs, but no 18.5.0 CHANGELOG names them. Two of them are declared breaking:

- **`ac0b9a5f9` (#33637).** Subject: `fix(plugin-audit)!: seal a window into checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows …`. Its changeset reads "Clause-②: yes (narrowing)": `os audit verify` reports a row id that two checkpoints list as the new chain fault `listed_twice` and fails the run, where the 18.4.0 verifier accepted it.
  - The published `@objectstack/plugin-audit@18.5.0` ships it: `listed_twice` appears in `dist/index.js`, `.mjs` and `.d.mts`.
  - Its `CHANGELOG.md` has 0 hits.
  - `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx` on main (`45dee177b`) has 0 hits for `listed_twice`, `checkpoint`, `#33637` and `#31908`.
- **`1e65a389e` (#33725, changeset `33689-ai-action-confirmation-elicited`).** The 18-5 page covers it ("Announced, not yet at any door"), but `@objectstack/spec@18.5.0`'s CHANGELOG has no line for it.

The other nine pending changesets at the tag:
- `33186-managed-add-people-actions`
- `33609-related-list-parent-lookup-page`
- `33649-messaging-preferences-emitting-organization`
- `33660-ai-model-picker-cost-multiplier`
- `33724-install-relaxes-declared-not-null`
- `33739-scenario-runner-effort`
- `33753-scenario-dates-follow-run-date`
- `33754-scenario-grader-written-date`
- `a2-skills-docs-32678-32825`

Coverage of the other breaking commits is good. Of the 63 `type(scope)!:` commits in `181ad7d4..b914e724`, the 18-5 page on main cites 62 by sha, including the org-scoped seed change `47a3b95e` / #33222. Only #33637 is missing.

**Reproduction:**
1. `git show b914e724:.changeset/31908-p4b2-bounded-checkpoints.md` shows the file still exists. `git merge-base --is-ancestor ac0b9a5f9 b914e724` is true. `git ls-tree --name-only b914e724 .changeset/`, minus README and config.json, lists 11 files.
2. `npm pack @objectstack/plugin-audit@18.5.0`. Then `grep -l listed_twice package/dist/*` finds 3 files, and `grep -c listed_twice package/CHANGELOG.md` gives 0.
3. `git show 45dee177b:content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx | grep -c -E 'listed_twice|ac0b9a5|33637'` gives 0.

- **Expected:** every change in the published 18.5.0 packages is named in its package's 18.5.0 CHANGELOG, and every `!` change is reachable from the 18-5 page.
- **Actual:** one shipped narrowing (`os audit verify` now fails a chain 18.4.0 accepted) is named nowhere in 18.5.0's notes, and ten more shipped changes are missing from the 18.5.0 CHANGELOGs.

Who is affected: an operator who runs `os audit verify` after upgrading can see a new failure that no release note explains.

**TO:**
- An 18.5.0 erratum on `18-5.mdx` naming #33637's FROM → TO: `os audit verify` used to pass a chain with a row listed in two checkpoints, and now fails it with `listed_twice`.
- The next version bump consumes the 11 changesets.
- Find out why the #29957 guard did not hold here. That guard says a Version Packages PR cannot land when main gained changesets after its branch point.

Same class as #29957 (18.3.0: a shipped narrowing with no CHANGELOG line, because the Version Packages PR was merged without regenerating). Docs and release process only. Not a security finding.

Dedupe: `gh api search/issues`, open and closed. No card exists for 18.5.0.
- `listed_twice` → #33773 (skills follow-up) and #31908 (epic), neither about the 18.5.0 notes.
- `31908-p4b2` → no match.
- `version packages changeset not consumed` → #29957, #25638 and #29933, all closed.
- `changesets pending at the release commit` → no match.
- `18.5.0 release page` → #33798 (closed; that card is the page itself).
